title: Unsigned Sysmon Driver and Process-Module Load Review
exclusions: Reviews Microsoft Sysmon event 6 driver loads and event 7 process-module loads only when the event reports `Signed=false`. It does not prove malware, rootkit activity, privilege escalation, DLL side-loading, signature revocation, or exploitation. It does not detect signed-but-vulnerable drivers, blocked loads, files never loaded, tampering before Sysmon starts, missing event-7 coverage, or every App Control/Code Integrity decision; use Microsoft vulnerable-driver blocklist/App Control, CodeIntegrity telemetry, EDR, and a maintained vulnerable-driver intelligence rule for those questions. Sysmon's signature is asynchronous, and absent/unavailable signature data needs file validation. This UC does not delete/quarantine a file, unload a driver/module, change Sysmon/App Control policy, isolate a host, or attest compliance.
evidence: After deployment, retain the `sysmon_unsigned_driver_module_load` saved-search definition, ACL, five-minute schedule, dispatch rows, and alerts; signed/hash-qualified Sysmon configuration and configuration-change evidence; Splunk Add-on for Sysmon input/knowledge configuration; raw event-6/7 XML with SHA-256; source-health/event-7 coverage output; versioned `sysmon_unsigned_load_exceptions.csv`; dashboard exports; file/signature/intelligence dispositions; and dated event-type, boundary, exception, duplicate, and delivery tests. Evidence proves Sysmon reported an unsigned load under the deployed configuration, not that the file was malicious. This documentation-only review generated no file load, Sysmon event, signature verification, search, alert, or production evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index, ingest one XML Sysmon event 6 at 2026-07-28T12:01:00Z with `source=XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational`, `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, `SourceName=Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon`, `host=win-lab-01`, `EventCode=6`, `ImageLoaded=C:\Lab\unsigned-test.sys`, `Hashes=SHA256=AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA`, `Signed=false`, `Signature=-`, and `SignatureStatus=Unavailable`; expect exactly one `driver` row with that lowercase SHA-256 and `event_count=1`. Repeat as event 7 with `Image=C:\Lab\loader.exe`, unique `ProcessGuid/ProcessId`, `ImageLoaded=C:\Lab\unsigned-test.dll`, and `User=LAB\tester`; expect one `module` row preserving process context.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Run separate fixtures and expect zero rows for event 6 or 7 with `Signed=true`; event 5 with `Signed=false`; wrong provider/source/source type; and unsigned data outside the complete ten-minute window. An event with `Signed=false` but no SHA-256 must not enter the primary alert and must appear in a separate data-quality search. A matching active exact `load_type,sha256,host,process_image` row in `sysmon_unsigned_load_exceptions.csv` may suppress delivery only after a base row exists; an expired row must not. Event 6 and 7 records sharing a hash remain separate load types.

dataSources: Microsoft Sysmon Operational event 6 (DriverLoad) and event 7 (ImageLoad) collected in XML by Splunk Add-on for Sysmon (Splunkbase 5709) from `[WinEventLog://Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational]`. Search `source=XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational, sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`; classic `source=WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational, sourcetype=WinEventLog` is accepted only after field qualification. Required fields are `_time, host, SourceName, EventCode, ImageLoaded, Hashes, Signed, Signature, SignatureStatus`; event 7 additionally requires `Image, ProcessGuid, ProcessId, User, OriginalFileName, Company`. SHA-256 collection is mandatory. `index=windows_sysmon` is the explicit local routing choice.
app: Splunk Add-on for Sysmon (`Splunk_TA_microsoft_sysmon`, Splunkbase 5709) for the dedicated Sysmon input, extractions, and CIM mappings. Microsoft Sysmon must be separately installed and governed on endpoints. A deployment-owned security-content app supplies this saved search, `sysmon_unsigned_load_exceptions.csv`, source/configuration-health searches, fixtures, dashboard, and response links.
spl:
index=windows_sysmon (source="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" OR source="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational") (sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog OR sourcetype=WinEventLog) SourceName="Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon" EventCode IN (6,7) Signed=false earliest=-10m@m latest=@m
| rex field=Hashes max_match=1 "(?i)(?:^|,)SHA256=(?<sha256>[A-F0-9]{64})(?:,|$)"
| eval sha256=lower(sha256), load_type=if(EventCode=6,"driver","module"), process_image=if(EventCode=7,coalesce(Image,"unknown"),"kernel_driver_context"), process_guid=if(EventCode=7,coalesce(ProcessGuid,"unknown"),"not_applicable"), process_id=if(EventCode=7,coalesce(ProcessId,"unknown"),"not_applicable"), load_user=if(EventCode=7,coalesce(User,"unknown"),"not_reported_for_driver")
| where len(sha256)=64
| stats count AS event_count earliest(_time) AS first_seen latest(_time) AS last_seen values(Signature) AS signatures values(SignatureStatus) AS signature_statuses values(Hashes) AS hashes values(process_guid) AS process_guids values(process_id) AS process_ids values(load_user) AS users values(OriginalFileName) AS original_file_names values(Company) AS companies by host load_type sha256 ImageLoaded process_image
| lookup sysmon_unsigned_load_exceptions.csv load_type sha256 host process_image OUTPUT exception_until reason AS exception_reason ticket owner
| eval exception_until_epoch=if(match(exception_until,"^\d+$"),tonumber(exception_until),strptime(exception_until,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")), exception_active=if(isnotnull(exception_until_epoch) AND exception_until_epoch>now(),1,0)
| where exception_active=0
| eval use_case_id="UC-1.2.129"
| convert ctime(first_seen) ctime(last_seen)
| sort 0 -last_seen host load_type ImageLoaded
description: Every five minutes, reviews the preceding ten complete minutes of Sysmon Operational event 6 and 7 data and emits one row for each host, driver/module load type, SHA-256, loaded path, and loading-process path where Sysmon reported `Signed=false`. One observed load is sufficient; counts and first/last time collapse duplicate observations without mixing driver and process-module semantics.
value: Unsigned code entering the kernel or an active process deserves prompt provenance review because it can expose privileged execution or module-search abuse. Hash- and process-rich results let responders distinguish approved legacy software from suspicious files while preserving the critical caveat that signed vulnerable drivers require separate prevention and detection.
implementation: Install and version Microsoft Sysmon, enable event 6 and narrowly governed event-7 collection with SHA-256 and signature metadata, and collect its Operational channel using Splunkbase 5709. Save the rule on a five-minute schedule over ten complete minutes; alert on each unsigned load without a count threshold. Investigate signature/file reputation, process and host context, Code Integrity/App Control state, and exact configuration coverage. Permit only exact, owner-approved, expiring hash/load/host/process exceptions after the base result is retained.
visualization: Security dashboard with Sysmon heartbeat/configuration and event-7 coverage first; current unsigned drivers above unsigned modules; tables by SHA-256, path, signer status, host, loading process, and owner; 24-hour trends; and drilldowns to raw XML, file reputation, CodeIntegrity/App Control evidence, process tree, and case disposition.
dataModelAcceleration: The Sysmon add-on maps events into CIM datasets, but the primary rule stays on raw events because it requires Sysmon `EventCode, Signed, SignatureStatus, Hashes, ImageLoaded, Image, ProcessGuid`. Qualify any accelerated replacement against the exact add-on/CIM version before use.

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Approved legacy hardware driver** — an OEM or line-of-business device may load an unsigned driver during an approved migration. Verify SHA-256 against the vendor-delivered package, procurement/change record, device model, file version, and independent malware scan; use the `lookup sysmon_unsigned_load_exceptions.csv` mechanism for a time-bound exact driver/hash/host/kernel-context exception while remediation is tracked.

2. **In-house unsigned development DLL** — a lab build may load into a signed or unsigned test process before release signing. Confirm repository/build pipeline, artifact digest, developer, lab asset, process path, and test window; allow only the exact module SHA-256, host, and process image until the build expires.

3. **Microsoft Visual Studio or test harness instrumentation** — controlled debugging/profiling can inject or load an unsigned module. Correlate `ProcessGuid`, process image, user, debugger/test job, and change ticket; suppress the exact tuple for the test duration, not all modules loaded by the tool.

4. **Endpoint security or forensics collection component** — a sanctioned EDR/forensics vendor can deploy a transient unsigned test component in validation environments. Confirm vendor case, package signature/digest, deployment ring, host owner, and removal time; use an exact expiring exception and independently verify production policy.

5. **Signature metadata unavailable or delayed** — Sysmon creates signature information asynchronously, and a removed file or validation issue can produce unavailable status. Retrieve the exact file if present, run approved Authenticode/catalog and reputation checks, compare SHA-256, and inspect CodeIntegrity events; do not permanently allow solely because the field is unavailable.

6. **Classic/XML or WEF duplicate ingestion** — one Sysmon record can arrive through overlapping local and forwarding inputs. Compare EventRecordID, UtcTime, host, source, sourcetype, and raw XML; repair collection. The aggregation can count duplicates but an exception must never hide telemetry duplication.

Every exception is post-detection, exact on `load_type,sha256,host,process_image`, owner/ticket/reason qualified, and expiring. Changed hash, process, host, load type, unknown SHA-256, configuration drift, and source-health failure remain visible.
reviewer: documentation-only Cursor AI editorial review against Microsoft Sysinternals Sysmon event-6/event-7 and configuration guidance, Microsoft vulnerable-driver block rules, Splunk Add-on for Sysmon and Security Content event samples, and MITRE ATT&CK T1068/T1574.002; Sysmon installation/configuration, event generation, signature/hash behavior, fixtures, SPL, coverage, exceptions, file analysis, alert delivery, containment, Windows/Sysmon/add-on/Splunk versions, and production response were specified but not executed or Microsoft/Splunk/Sysinternals/endpoint/detection-engineering/SOC/SME signed
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and detection boundary

Assign endpoint engineering, Windows platform, Sysmon configuration, application/driver, code-signing, Splunk data, detection engineering, threat intelligence, SOC, incident-response, and change owners. Install Microsoft Sysmon through a governed endpoint process and use a currently supported Splunk Add-on for Sysmon (Splunkbase 5709) release qualified against the deployment. This documentation-only review ran no version combination, so it asserts no `splunkVersions`. The forwarder needs read access to the Sysmon Operational channel and transport only. Search/respond roles need the Sysmon index, lookup read, schedule/action rights, and separately approved file/EDR access. Restrict Sysmon policy, lookup, containment, and App Control changes.

Microsoft defines event 6 as a loaded driver with configured hashes and signature information. Event 7 records a module loaded into a specific process with process, hash, and signature details; it is disabled by default and Microsoft warns that unfiltered image-load monitoring generates significant volume. Sysmon creates signature information asynchronously. Therefore `Signed=false` is a review fact, not a malware verdict. One load fires; no count threshold applies. Event 6 has no loading-process fields comparable to event 7, so the SPL labels its process context `kernel_driver_context` instead of inventing an image.

This rule intentionally does not detect signed vulnerable drivers. Microsoft explains that actors exploit legitimate signed kernel drivers and recommends the vulnerable-driver blocklist/HVCI or App Control policy, with audit testing before enforcement because blocking can malfunction or blue-screen systems. Maintain separate prevention posture and hash/intelligence detection. T1068 and T1574.002 are investigation mappings: an unsigned driver or module alone does not prove exploitation or DLL side-loading.

## Step 1 — Configure Sysmon and Splunk collection

Version-control the Sysmon XML, deployment ring, binary/config hashes, schema version, effective time, and owner. Ensure `HashAlgorithms` includes SHA256. Event 6 must be enabled. Enable event 7 only with reviewed include/exclude rules based on threat model and representative volume; Microsoft documents the `-l` option and warns against indiscriminate collection. Do not copy a path allowlist that excludes Windows/System32 or Program Files from this search: malicious or unsigned modules can load there, and path alone is not trust.

Apply configuration through approved Sysmon tooling and preserve event 16 configuration-change records plus `sysmon -c`/configuration evidence appropriate to the environment. Pilot event 7 by workstation/server role, measure events/second, CPU, event-log retention, forwarder queues, ingest, and search cost. Define required process/path coverage and expected host population. A host without event 7 cannot be represented as having no unsigned module loads.

Deploy Splunkbase 5709 according to its supported input/search-tier topology. Configure `[WinEventLog://Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational]` with XML rendering and route to the explicit local `index=windows_sysmon`. Verify `source=XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational, sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`. The SPL accepts classic source/type only after qualification. Confirm `SourceName=Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon`, event 6/7, `ImageLoaded, Hashes, Signed, Signature, SignatureStatus`; confirm event-7 `Image, ProcessGuid, ProcessId, User, OriginalFileName, Company`. Compare raw examples with Splunk Security Content samples.

Create `sysmon_unsigned_load_exceptions.csv` with `load_type,sha256,host,process_image,exception_until,reason,ticket,owner`. Use lowercase 64-character SHA-256, exact canonical host and process image, UTC expiry, and one reviewed tuple per row. Event-6 process value is exactly `kernel_driver_context`. Reject wildcard-only/permanent entries. Create separate searches for missing SHA-256, absent signature fields, duplicate events, event-7 coverage, host heartbeat, event 16 changes, config hash drift, and expired/invalid exceptions.

## Step 2 — Create the saved search and alert

Save the sidecar SPL as `sysmon_unsigned_driver_module_load`; run every five minutes over the preceding ten complete minutes (`earliest=-10m@m latest=@m`) to tolerate ordinary indexing delay. The base search locks index, exact Sysmon source/source type, provider, event IDs, and `Signed=false`. `rex` extracts only a comma-delimited 64-hex `SHA256=` value. Events without one are routed by the separate data-quality search and cannot create a primary hash-based case.

`eval` separates `driver` from `module` semantics and supplies explicit not-applicable values. `stats` produces one host/load/hash/loaded-path/loading-process row and preserves signatures, statuses, configured hash string, process GUID/ID, user, original filename, and company. Apply the exact exception lookup only after aggregation. Trigger per result and throttle on `host,load_type,sha256,ImageLoaded,process_image` for ten minutes. Continue displaying counts because duplicate loads, repeated process instances, or overlapping collection matter to investigation.

Alert title: `Sysmon reported unsigned <driver|module> load on <host>`. Include SHA-256, paths, process identifiers, signer/status, first/last UTC, count, user, Sysmon/config coverage, exception outcome, asset owner/criticality, file-intelligence links, and runbook. Do not automatically delete, quarantine, unload, kill, block, or isolate. Driver action can destabilize the kernel; module/process action can destroy evidence or disrupt production.

## Step 3 — Validate data, semantics, and scale

Run every `controlTest` fixture in an isolated index with fixed dispatch. Test event 6 and 7, `Signed=false` string/case actually produced by the add-on, `Signed=true`, wrong provider/event/source/source type, SHA-256 first/middle/last among configured hashes, lowercase/uppercase digest, absent/malformed digest, complete-window edges, active/expired/malformed exception, driver/module same hash, event-7 process fields, and event-6 not-applicable context. Assert exact output grain and preserved fields.

In an isolated Windows lab, use benign purpose-built signed and unsigned test artifacts only if endpoint/security owners approve. Load a test driver only in a disposable VM with snapshot/console recovery and vendor-approved method; a bad driver can crash Windows. Prefer fixture replay for event 6. For event 7, use a harmless test process/module and compare **Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > Sysmon > Operational** raw XML with Splunk. Verify SHA-256 externally, check Authenticode/catalog status with approved Windows tooling, and observe asynchronous signature behavior. Never weaken production signing/App Control to generate data.

Measure event-7 volume and coverage across representative roles. Run hourly counts by host/event ID, compare expected hosts/config hashes, inspect event-log drops/retention, `_indextime-_time`, forwarder queues, search runtime, scheduler skips, and duplicate routes. Exercise alert delivery, throttle, lookup replication/expiry, dashboard, file-retrieval permissions, case enrichment, and response handoff. Keep `status=draft` until owners approve tested Windows/Sysmon/add-on/Splunk versions, configuration, fields, event-7 scope, volume, fixtures, source/config health, exceptions, alerting, and response.

## Step 4 — Investigate and operationalize

Dashboard order: expected-host Sysmon heartbeat and config drift; event-6 coverage; event-7 enabled-scope coverage; unsigned drivers; unsigned modules; missing hashes/signatures; top SHA-256/path/process; exceptions nearing expiry; and dispositions. Show loaded-path and loading-process separately. Restrict raw events and artifact access. Retain raw XML/EventRecordID, Sysmon config/version, file SHA-256/signature/catalog metadata, search/lookup revisions, dispatch, EDR/file-intelligence results, change/vendor evidence, alert/case actions, and closure evidence under security policy.

Responder sequence: (1) verify source, provider, event ID, host, load type, hash extraction, paths, process context, signature fields, event/config health, and exception; (2) obtain the file safely or query EDR by exact SHA-256 without executing it; (3) verify Authenticode/catalog chain, timestamp, revocation result, publisher, file version, and hash reputation; (4) correlate process tree, file creation/download, service/driver install, CodeIntegrity/App Control, Defender/EDR, network, user, change, and neighboring Sysmon events; (5) for drivers, check Microsoft vulnerable-driver blocklist and vendor security notices even if unsigned status is the trigger; (6) determine approved legacy/test, invalid signature, suspicious module, vulnerable driver, or confirmed incident; (7) contain through endpoint/incident procedures with service and crash planning; (8) remove/upgrade/block only under reviewed change; and (9) validate source/config health and no recurrence. A signed replacement is not automatically safe; verify version and policy.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot safely

- **No event 6:** verify Sysmon installed/running, effective DriverLoad configuration, Operational channel retention, input stanza, forwarder, index routing, and permissions. Compare config and event 16 changes.
- **No event 7:** Microsoft disables it by default. Verify effective ImageLoad configuration and deployment scope; do not label unconfigured hosts clean.
- **Event 7 overwhelms ingest:** refine Sysmon include/exclude policy by threat model and process/path/signature evidence, pilot again, and preserve coverage documentation. Do not add broad SPL-only exclusions that already consumed ingest.
- **`Signed` or `SignatureStatus` missing:** inspect raw XML, Sysmon schema/version, asynchronous signing behavior, add-on extraction, and removed file. Route to data-quality review rather than assuming false or true.
- **SHA-256 missing:** ensure Sysmon `HashAlgorithms` includes SHA256, inspect `Hashes`, schema, config drift, and add-on fields. The primary rule rejects the event but source-health must alert.
- **Driver row has no process:** expected event-6 contract; investigate service/driver installation and neighboring events instead of inventing a loader.
- **File path is trusted-looking:** do not suppress on `System32` or Program Files alone. Validate exact hash, signer/catalog, version, change, and intelligence.
- **Signed vulnerable driver not found:** expected exclusion. Use Microsoft/App Control blocklist posture, CodeIntegrity/EDR, and a dedicated vulnerable-driver hash/certificate rule.
- **Duplicate count:** compare EventRecordID/UtcTime, WEF/local routes, source/type, and schedule overlap; fix collection or notification identity without hiding a genuine load.
- **Exception mismatch:** normalize lowercase SHA-256 and exact load/host/process values, check UTC expiry, lookup definition/ACL/replication, and rerun. Never broaden to wildcard solely to silence volume.
grandmaExplanation: We watch when Windows loads a driver or a piece of code that the system reports as unsigned. Some old or in-house software can do this legitimately, but the exact file and the program using it should be checked before it is trusted.
